'''Morton Brown''' (August 12, 1931 – August 3, 2024<ref name="obituary" />) was an American mathematician who specialized in [[geometric topology]].

==Life and career==
Brown was born in New York City on August 12, 1931. In 1958 Brown earned his Ph.D. from the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]] under [[R. H. Bing]]. From 1960 to 1962 he was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]]. Afterwards he became a professor at the [[University of Michigan at Ann Arbor]].<ref name="Memorials">{{cite web |title=Memorials |url=https://lsa.umich.edu/math/people/memorials.html |website=lsa.umich.edu |access-date=16 July 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

With [[Barry Mazur]] in 1965 he won the [[Oswald Veblen prize]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/prizes-awards/ams-prizes/veblen-prize|title = Oswald Veblen Prize in Geometry}}</ref> for their independent and nearly simultaneous proofs of the [[Schönflies problem|generalized Schoenflies hypothesis]]<ref>{{cite journal |author=Brown, Morton |year=1960 |title= A proof of the generalized Schoenflies theorem |journal= Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. |volume=66 |issue=2 |pages=74–76 |doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1960-10400-4|doi-access=free }} {{MathSciNet| id = 0117695}}</ref> in geometric topology. Brown's short proof was elementary and fully general. Mazur's proof was also elementary, but it used a special assumption which was removed via later work of Morse.{{Citation needed|date=July 2025}}

In the late 1980s, Brown implemented a large reform to the calculus classes taught at the University of Michigan. His changes later became a model for a national calculus reform movement.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celebratio Mathematica — Brown — Curriculum Vitae |url=https://celebratio.org/Brown_Morton/article/682/ |website=celebratio.org |access-date=16 July 2025}}</ref><ref name="Memorials"/>

In 2012 he became an inaugural fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref>
